chunks: From him, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ al-Munabbih ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

We were with him, and he heard the iqamah of a neighbor of his for the salat (prayer), so he said, “Rise.” So we rose and prayed with him without an adhan or iqamah. He said, “The adhan of your neighbor suffices you.”

key_terms.إِقَامَةٍ: the second call before beginning the salat (prayer)
key_terms.إِقَامَةَ: the call signaling the immediate commencement of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.جَارٍ: a nearby neighbor whose adhan or iqamah is heard
key_terms.يُجْزِيكُمْ: is sufficient for you; fulfills the needed requirement

ai.seo_question: Does the adhan of a nearby neighbor suffice for one’s own salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that when the adhan has already been called nearby, it can suffice for others joining the salat (prayer) without repeating the adhan and iqamah. It relates to the jurisprudence of congregational worship and shows facilitation in shared communal prayer settings.
